title: ISO/IEC 27002:2022: the four themes of the controls and the values of the five attributes, in our own words

controls.title: Organizational controls
controls.statement: Controls on how the organization governs and runs security: policies, roles, assets, access, suppliers, incidents, continuity and compliance. In Annex A they are the first 37.

controls.title: People controls
controls.statement: Controls on the people who work for or with the organization: screening, terms, awareness, discipline, remote work and reporting. In Annex A they are 8 controls.

controls.title: Physical controls
controls.statement: Controls on places and equipment: perimeters, entry, monitoring, environmental threats, utilities, cabling, maintenance and disposal. In Annex A they are 14 controls.

controls.title: Technological controls
controls.statement: Controls on systems and networks: endpoints, privileged access, authentication, malware, vulnerabilities, configuration, logging, network security, cryptography and secure development. In Annex A they are 34 controls.

controls.title: Preventive
controls.statement: The control acts before an event, to keep it from happening.

controls.title: Detective
controls.statement: The control acts when an event happens, to notice it.

controls.title: Corrective
controls.statement: The control acts after an event, to limit its effect and restore.

controls.title: Confidentiality
controls.statement: The control serves keeping information from those who may not see it.

controls.title: Integrity
controls.statement: The control serves keeping information accurate and whole.

controls.title: Availability
controls.statement: The control serves keeping information and services usable when needed.

controls.title: Identify
controls.statement: The control helps the organization know its assets, risks and context.

controls.title: Protect
controls.statement: The control helps put safeguards in place.

controls.title: Detect
controls.statement: The control helps find events as they happen.

controls.title: Respond
controls.statement: The control helps act on an event.

controls.title: Recover
controls.statement: The control helps restore what an event disturbed.

controls.title: Governance
controls.statement: The capability of setting direction and holding people to it.

controls.title: Asset management
controls.statement: The capability of knowing and looking after assets.

controls.title: Information protection
controls.statement: The capability of protecting information by its kind.

controls.title: Human resource security
controls.statement: The capability of managing security across the working life of people.

controls.title: Physical security
controls.statement: The capability of protecting places and equipment.

controls.title: System and network security
controls.statement: The capability of securing systems and the networks that join them.

controls.title: Application security
controls.statement: The capability of building and running secure applications.

controls.title: Secure configuration
controls.statement: The capability of setting up and keeping systems in a secure state.

controls.title: Identity and access management
controls.statement: The capability of knowing who and what may reach what.

controls.title: Threat and vulnerability management
controls.statement: The capability of finding and acting on threats and weaknesses.

controls.title: Continuity
controls.statement: The capability of carrying on through disruption.

controls.title: Supplier relationships security
controls.statement: The capability of keeping security across the suppliers the organization depends on.

controls.title: Legal and compliance
controls.statement: The capability of meeting the rules that apply.

controls.title: Information security event management
controls.statement: The capability of handling events and incidents.

controls.title: Information security assurance
controls.statement: The capability of showing that security works.

controls.title: Governance and ecosystem
controls.statement: The domain of security governance and of the relations with others in the ecosystem.

controls.title: Protection
controls.statement: The domain of safeguards that protect assets.

controls.title: Defence
controls.statement: The domain of detecting and responding to attacks.

controls.title: Resilience
controls.statement: The domain of withstanding and recovering from adverse events.

publisher: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)
